name: Read a subway or transit map quickly
blurb: Transit maps are schematic diagrams, not geography. Understanding that, plus a few reading habits, gets you around any new city’s network in minutes.
gear: A transit map — paper or app
steps: Understand the abstraction: the map preserves topology and order, not distance or direction. Two stations close on the map can be far apart in reality.
Learn to identify interchanges and how they are marked, since journey planning is mostly about choosing where to change.
Learn to read direction: lines are labelled by their terminus, so you need the end-of-line name, not the compass direction.
Learn the zone or fare structure before travelling, and how to buy the right ticket.
Plan a multi-change journey on paper and then walk it.
Learn to spot when walking is faster — adjacent stations are often five minutes apart on foot.
tips: Always check the terminus on the platform indicator. Boarding the right line in the wrong direction is the classic mistake.
Check whether your interchange requires leaving the paid area, which can mean a second fare.
proof: You plan and execute a three-change journey in an unfamiliar city without hesitating at any platform.
